evidence_for_A: Date regex uses '\b' after the day which fails the requirement that dates not be followed by alphanumeric OR hyphen (only handles word chars, and the leading (?:19|20) year restriction is not required by task and may miss valid years)
Uses '\b((?:19|20)\d{2})' restricting years to 19xx/20xx which is arbitrary and could reject valid test years
evidence_for_B: Uses '(?![\w-])' after date to prevent alphanumeric AND hyphen following the date, matching the task's false-match requirement (e.g., 1134-12-1234)
Full 4-octet IPv4 with no-leading-zero octets and word boundaries
Negative lookahead ensures only the last date on a line is matched
Uses \d{4} for year without arbitrary century restriction
result.reason: Attempt B's patch passes the verifier and correctly handles the alphanumeric/hyphen boundary constraint via (?![\w-]), the last-date-only requirement, and IPv4 validation. Attempt A failed the test, only guarded word boundaries (not hyphens) after the date, and imposed an arbitrary year restriction.
